newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI 14 to place four companies on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI 14 to place four companies on bourse.

text.p: Polish National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 14 plans to place four of its companies on the Warsaw bourse this year or early next, the fund's spokeswoman said on Thursday.
Katarzyna Majrzak told Reuters that two issue prospectuses are likely to reach the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) in May and two others in October or November.
"We plan to hand in prospectuses of four firms this year," she said.
Majrzak also said the NFI, which goes by the name of Zachodni, planned to sell its 33-percent stakes in five companies, but declined to name them.
Under Poland's mass privatisaton NFI programme, shares in some 500 medium-size companies were allocated to 15 NFIs, which are run by foreign and domestic management firms.

About 26 million Poles bought their participation unit in the programme for a nominal fee in a sale that ended last November. The NFIs are expected to enter the Warsaw Stock Exchange in the third quarter of 1997.
NFI Zachodni made a net loss of 14.6 million zlotys in the first nine months of 1996 on 894.6 million zlotys in sales.
